slides.texte_overlay:
how to sound smart
without trying too hard

ask good questions

ask how and why more than you share your own opinion. curious, specific questions make you sound more thoughtful than any clever statement ever could.

use simple words

explain things in the simplest words you can. people who truly understand something can always make it sound simple, and everyone else can quietly tell.

know a little of everything

spend 5 minutes a day learning about something new: art, history, the stars. knowing a little about many things lets you join any conversation with ease.
slides.texte_sophia:
know a little of everything

i spend 5 minutes a day learning something new: art, history, the stars. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and knowing a little about many things helps everywhere.

slides.texte_overlay:
admit what you don't know

say i'm not sure, but i think, instead of pretending. honest uncertainty sounds far more intelligent than confident guesses that later turn out wrong.

listen fully

let people finish before you answer, and refer back to what they said. listening carefully is the quietest and most underrated way to sound genuinely smart.
